questions.title: Direct Binomial Probability for Exactly Two Successes

parts.text: The random variable $X$ has the distribution $B(6, 0.4)$. Find the value of $P(X = 2)$, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

A seed germinates with probability $0.28$, independently of other seeds. Five seeds are planted. Find the probability that exactly two seeds germinate, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Combined Categories: All Four Trials Successful

parts.text: On any day, a train is early with probability $0.12$, on time with probability $0.60$, and late with probability $0.28$. The arrivals on different days are independent. Find the probability that on each of 4 randomly chosen days, the train is not late.

questions.title: Using the Complement for At Least Two Wins

parts.text: A player wins each game with probability $0.25$, independently of other games. The player plays 8 games. Find the probability of winning at least 2 games, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Exact Binomial Term for Rolling a Standard Die

parts.text: A standard fair 6-sided die is rolled 5 times. Find the probability of obtaining a score of 4 on exactly 3 of the rolls, giving your answer as an exact fraction.

questions.title: Sum of Two Exact Tail Terms

parts.text: The random variable $X$ has the distribution $B(7, 0.2)$. Find $P(X \le 1)$, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.

questions.title: Exact and At Least One Success in Five Trials

parts.text: The random variable $X$ has the distribution $B(5, 0.35)$. Find $P(X = 2)$, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
Find the probability of obtaining at least one success, $P(X \ge 1)$.

A student guesses the answer to each of 6 multiple-choice questions independently. Each question has 4 options, exactly one of which is correct. Find the probability that the student guesses exactly 3 questions correctly.
To pass the test, the student must answer at least 4 questions correctly. Find the probability that the student passes by guessing.

questions.title: Range of Values and Strict Tail Probability

parts.text: The random variable $X$ has the distribution $B(10, 0.6)$. Find the probability that $X$ lies in the inclusive interval $5 \le X \le 7$, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
Find the probability that $X$ is strictly greater than 8, $P(X > 8)$.

questions.title: Quality Control: Batch Inspection of Flawed Items

parts.text: A manufacturing process produces flawed components with a constant probability of $0.08$. A random sample of 12 components is selected for inspection. Find the probability that exactly one component in the sample is flawed.
Find the probability that at most 2 components in the sample are flawed.

questions.title: Archery Competition: Tail and Conditional Probabilities

parts.text: An archer hits the bullseye with probability $0.45$ on each shot, independently of all other shots. The archer releases 7 arrows. Find the probability that the archer hits the bullseye at least 5 times.
Given that the archer hits the bullseye at least 5 times, find the conditional probability that the archer hits the bullseye exactly 6 times.

questions.title: Two-Stage Binomial: Batch Acceptance and Compound Repetitions

parts.text: In a factory, $15\%$ of manufactured components are defective. A box contains a random sample of 9 components. Find the probability that a box contains exactly 2 defective components, giving your answer correct to 3 significant figures.
A box is accepted for shipping if it contains at most 1 defective component. Show that the probability that a randomly chosen box is accepted is $0.599$, correct to 3 significant figures.
A consignment consists of 5 independent boxes. Find the probability that at least 4 of the 5 boxes are accepted for shipping.

questions.title: Airline Overbooking Model: Cumulative, Complement, and Conditional Probabilities

parts.text: An airline operates a small aircraft with 8 passenger seats. Historical data indicates that $80\%$ of ticket holders show up for their flight, independently of one another. The airline sells 10 tickets for a scheduled flight. Let $X$ be the number of passengers who show up. Find the probability that the flight is overbooked (meaning more than 8 passengers show up).
Find the probability that at least one seat on the aircraft remains empty.
Given that at least 8 passengers show up, find the conditional probability that every passenger who shows up gets a seat.
